derived_vs_estimate_among_existed_true.note: Every completed existence check in this corpus used the exact (DERIVED) git-checkout method (D-C); the ESTIMATE fallback (date-filter, used when git history doesn't reach the moment's timestamp) was never actually needed -- 0/147. tier1_no_search_decomposition.question: Tier-1 measurement: for the 98 moments where search_ran=='none' (no agent-initiated memory search), what is the grade distribution for the relevance of existing vault memories? Two-stage judgment: (1) sonnet relevance grading, (2) strict counterfactual arbitration to verify the initial grades would have changed the agent's action.
tier1_no_search_decomposition.label: DERIVED (audited sample measurements from 54 transcripts; Tier-1 provenance 'sonnet relevance-grading-v3')

denominator.definition: all moments with search_ran=='none' (no search was invoked; memory may or may not have existed)

initial_grades.note: Initial judgment: relevance grade assigned by sonnet over the retrieved top-5 search results for the moment's window. Grades: relevant_top1 (the best match directly answers the need), relevant_in_top5 (a relevant hit exists but not rank 1), nothing_relevant (top-5 contains no memory that bears on the moment's question). Counted among the 96 judged moments (2 were skipped due to data unavailability).

post_arbitration.note: Strict counterfactual arbitration: an initial 'relevant' grade was overturned if an adversarial verifier judged that the memory, had it been surfaced to the agent, would NOT have changed the agent's action (false would_have_changed_action). All 6 initially-relevant moments were subject to arbitration: 1 survived (would_have_changed_action==true), 5 were overturned (would_have_changed_action==false). This is a strict measure of 'memory whose absence directly caused loss', not a looser 'relevance to the general topic' measure.

fire_cue.note: fire_cue classifies WHY no search ran. 'not_a_recall_moment': the moment is not a decision point where a recall fire-unit should trigger (e.g., success moments, dispatch moments). 'cue_present_missed': a recall fire-unit SHOULD have fired (e.g., task initialization, failure diagnosis) but the cue was not detected in the transcript. 'no_cue_exists': no appropriate recall fire-unit exists for this moment type. Among the 22 cue_present_missed moments, the cue_name breakdown shows which fire-unit types were missed.

tier1_no_search_decomposition.joint_note: All 6 initially-relevant moments (relevant_top1 or relevant_in_top5) were classified fire_cue='cue_present_missed' -- they are moments where the recall system should have fired a memory search but did not (task-initialization, failure-diagnosis, etc.). Post-arbitration, exactly 1 of the full corpus (1/150 total moments) qualifies as 'relevant memory existed, cue was missed, AND it would have changed the action' -- labeled DERIVED in the above findings. The other 5 initially-relevant moments are classified as 'high-quality memory exists, but surfacing it would not have altered the agent's decision' (verdict: not a loss boundary; interesting for understanding vault coverage, not for measuring recall efficacy against the primary gate in #739).

fire_unit.label: ESTIMATE
fire_unit.caveat: Hit counts come from the AUDITED SAMPLE only: 150 detected moments across 54 audited transcripts, of which 98 no-search moments were measured here (96 judged, 2 skipped). Corpus-wide hit numbers extrapolate the per-transcript sample rate to the 568-transcript corpus (x10.52) and assume the audited transcripts are representative -- they are labeled ESTIMATE, not measured. Detected moments are themselves a lower bound (the moment detector is not exhaustive). Per-failure-event fires corpus-wide are also extrapolated (moments exist only for the audited sample).
